articles.title: Rochdale Council Staff Win North West Trisector Challenge
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council staff have triumphed in the North West Employers Trisector Challenge, outperforming 13 local authorities to secure a prestigious award.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council staff have won the North West Employers Trisector Challenge, beating 13 other local authorities to secure the top award. The competition, which took place at Halliwell Jones Stadium in Warrington, aimed to provide aspiring leaders with exposure to cross-sector issues and insights into senior management roles.

Teams participating in the challenge were required to collaborate with neighbouring stakeholders and partners to develop a new strategy for their organisations. They faced the task of prioritising key areas, addressing politically sensitive issues, and maintaining a customer-focused approach while delivering public services amid limited resources.

Following the victory, the Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana, praised the efforts of the council staff, stating, "Well done to all the staff at Rochdale Borough Council for winning the North West Trisector Challenge!" This recognition highlights the council's commitment to effective service delivery and innovative problem-solving.

The win not only reflects the hard work of the council staff but also sets a benchmark for future initiatives aimed at enhancing public service delivery in the borough. It remains to be seen how this achievement will influence ongoing projects and collaborations within the local government framework.

articles.title: Masdar Launches 35 MW/70 MWh Battery Energy Storage System in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Masdar has commenced commercial operations at its new battery energy storage system in Rochdale, which is expected to support grid stability and supply power to approximately 35,000 homes daily.
articles.content_html:
Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC, known as Masdar, has officially started commercial operations at its 35 MW/70 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) located in Rochdale, UK. This facility marks Masdar's second operational battery storage project in the country and is part of a broader £1 billion investment programme aimed at enhancing battery energy storage capabilities in the UK.

The Rochdale BESS is designed to provide sufficient clean energy to power around 35,000 homes each day, based on two charging and discharging cycles. Additionally, the system will offer grid-balancing services, responding to fluctuations in electricity supply and demand within milliseconds, thereby supporting overall grid stability and facilitating greater integration of renewable energy sources into the UK electricity network.

Masdar's commitment to the UK market follows its acquisition of Arlington Energy in 2022, with plans to develop a pipeline of battery storage projects totalling 3 GWh. This initiative aligns with the UK government's Clean Power 2030 Action Plan, which aims for up to 27 GW of battery storage capacity by the end of the decade. The Rochdale project complements Masdar's existing 20 MW/40 MWh facility in Stockport, which began operations in December 2025, and additional projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff, totalling 150 MW/300 MWh.

The new facility incorporates advanced safety features, including fire detection and suppression systems, 24-hour CCTV monitoring, and local response capabilities. As battery energy storage systems play a crucial role in managing electricity supply during periods of low demand and discharging during peak demand, this project is expected to significantly contribute to the UK's energy security and sustainability efforts.

articles.title: Northern Care Alliance Staff Strike Over Overtime Payments at Rochdale Infirmary
articles.excerpt: Over 350 staff from the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust are striking over overtime payment disputes, affecting services at Rochdale Infirmary and other hospitals.
articles.content_html:
Hundreds of operating theatre staff from the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust returned to the picket lines this morning as part of a three-day strike over overtime payments. More than 350 members of the Unison union, employed at Rochdale Infirmary, Salford Royal Hospital, Fairfield General Hospital, and Royal Oldham Hospital, are participating in the industrial action due to disputes regarding overtime compensation.

The strike centres on the issue of time-and-a-half payments that staff are entitled to when covering for staff shortages. Unison claims that the use of agency staff has resulted in some trust employees earning less than they would on a normal shift, with some missing out on over £80 per shift. This has led to significant discontent among the workforce, prompting the current strike action.

In response to the ongoing dispute, hospital management has declared a critical incident, allowing them to bring in additional support to maintain urgent surgical services. However, some procedures are expected to be postponed as theatre staff, including nurses and clinical support workers, join the picket lines. This follows a previous strike in June, which was called off after an agreement appeared to be reached, but Unison stated that the offer was later withdrawn.

Kevin Dolan, a regional organiser for Unison, expressed frustration over the situation, stating that the leadership at the Northern Care Alliance has shown a lack of regard for their staff. The trust has acknowledged the challenges it faces and is working to address concerns while focusing on improving safety and care standards. The outcome of this strike could have significant implications for staffing and patient care at local hospitals.
